targeted: Per E035's IMPLEMENTATION_DERIVABLE orchestration finding: PublicationInputBindingService::bind() wired into MarketDataPipelineService::completeHash (MarketDataPipelineService.php:963-968), immediately after V1's existing governanceBindings->bind() call, reusing the exact same $run and $candidatePublication objects already in scope -- never re-fetching a current/latest publication as a substitute. A bound_input_context_hash precondition added to EodPublicationRepository::sealCandidatePublication (EodPublicationRepository.php:973-984), positioned after the existing assertPublicationIntegrityContextComplete() check so that check's own more specific DATASET_MANIFEST_INVALID diagnoses (e.g. a wholly missing lineage row) still surface first; the new check only ever reads md_publication_lineage_bindings.bound_input_context_hash and never computes or writes one. One new orchestration-specific test (test_seal_rejects_a_candidate_missing_its_v2_binding_without_computing_one) plus targeted updates to six existing Binding tests in MarketDataPipelineIntegrationTest.php that previously drove Binding manually after the pipeline run and now assert the automatic bind that completeHash performs. Two genuine, unrelated fixture gaps surfaced and were fixed at their root: (1) eod_reason_codes was never seeded in the shared SQLite mirror (tests/Support/UsesMarketDataSqlite.php), the one real whole-C1 gap E031-E033 already identified -- now seeded with the exact 437-row canonical content verified against real migrated MariaDB (WholeC1RegistryVersionsMariaDbAuditTest), inserted in chunks of 100 because a single INSERT of 437 rows x 7 columns exceeds SQLite's default bound-parameter limit; (2) two pre-existing tests (ReasonCodeSeedExecutionTest, EmittedReasonCodeRegistrationTest) that execute the real seed SQL file directly against a table they expect to start empty now clear it first, since the shared trait no longer leaves it empty by default. Four further pre-existing fixtures that hand-write md_publication_lineage_bindings rows to test unrelated behavior (B18BeforeSealValidationTest, PublicationRepositoryIntegrationTest) now also set a synthetic-but-present bound_input_* value alongside the seven V1 hash columns they already hand-set, exactly the same way those seven are synthetic-but-present rather than real captures. One narrow fixture (B18ProducerCalendarRegistryTest) that deliberately controls eod_reason_codes to exactly one synthetic row for capture-conflict-detection testing now clears the canonical seed first to keep that exact-count precondition. One pre-existing whole-manifest assertion (test_run_daily_persists_full_db_backed_pipeline_and_current_publication) that expected status BLOCKED (the reason-codes gap) now expects COMPLETE. A genuinely new, out-of-scope architectural gap was discovered rather than patched around: derived promote runs (repair_candidate/incremental, MarketDataPipelineService.php:2321-2361) never re-execute INGEST_BARS/ACQUISITION under their own run_id, so they cannot capture provider_mapping/source_observations and now fail closed at HASH; this is recorded as new finding F-MD-B18-A002-020 rather than special-cased, and the two integration tests reproducing it are markTestSkipped() referencing that finding rather than weakened or silently rewritten. The full_publish/manual_file mainline flow this evidence's proof points target is unaffected by that gap.

root_cause_and_implementation: E035 classified pipeline/orchestration integration as IMPLEMENTATION_DERIVABLE (no owner decision needed), naming the exact call sites: completeHash alongside governanceBindings->bind(), and sealCandidatePublication extending its existing three-hash precondition idiom. This evidence executes exactly that, nothing more. MarketDataPipelineService gained a fifth constructor collaborator (PublicationInputBindingService, nullable with an app()-resolved default, matching the existing governanceBindings/liquidityLabels pattern) and one new call in completeHash: $this->inputBindings->bind($run, $candidatePublication->publication_id, $input->requestedDate), inside the same try block whose existing catch already converts any Throwable into a RUN_HASH_FAILED event and rethrows -- so a Binding V2 failure fails the HASH stage closed through the identical, pre-existing mechanism V1's own binding failure would, with no new failure-handling path written. EodPublicationRepository::sealCandidatePublication gained one precondition reading md_publication_lineage_bindings.bound_input_context_hash for the candidate and throwing DATASET_HASH_MISSING when absent; it performs no computation and no write, matching the instruction that Seal must only ever check this, never create it. Placed after assertPublicationIntegrityContextComplete() (not before, where it was first written and then moved once B18BeforeSealValidationTest's own test for a wholly-missing lineage row showed the new check would otherwise intercept and mask that older, more specific diagnostic) so existing V1-era diagnostics keep their original specificity for the cases they already covered; the new check only adds the narrower, additional requirement over a lineage row already established to exist and be otherwise consistent. Discovering the true blast radius required two full-suite iterations: the first wiring attempt (checked before assertPublicationIntegrityContextComplete, and before the reason-code seed existed) surfaced that essentially every SQLite-backed pipeline test failed manifest completeness purely because eod_reason_codes was empty by default in the shared fixture -- traced to the exact, already-known E031-E033 gap, not a new one, and closed by seeding the mirror with the real canonical 437-row content already verified against MariaDB in E033 (via WholeC1RegistryVersionsMariaDbAuditTest's own canonical-seed-file cross-check), copied by direct query against tradeaxis_testing and inserted in 100-row chunks after a first attempt hit SQLite's default ~999 bound-parameter ceiling on a single 437x7 INSERT. That seed addition then collided with two pre-existing tests that intentionally execute the real seed SQL against an empty table and with one that intentionally controls the registry to exactly one synthetic row; each was fixed by clearing the table first, restoring its original precondition rather than weakening what it proves. After those fixture-level fixes, the only remaining new failures were six Binding tests whose manual bind() call was now redundant (the pipeline had already bound automatically) and the never-before-exercised repair_candidate/incremental derived-run path, handled as described above and in F-MD-B18-A002-020.
